subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Repeating a short melodic pattern at higher or lower pitches in turn is called a:
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic idea at successively higher or lower pitches.

options: Changing the dynamics of a piece
Moving music up or down to a different pitch or key
questions.explain: Transposition moves a piece of music to a higher or lower pitch (a different key).

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

options: Composing music to meet a given set of requirements or purpose
questions.explain: Composing to a brief means writing music that fulfils a specified purpose or set of instructions.

questions.q: 'Imitation' as a way of developing an idea means:
options: One part copies a melodic idea just stated by another part
questions.explain: Imitation is when one part copies a melodic idea introduced by another part.

questions.q: In a melody-and-accompaniment texture, the accompaniment:
options: Supports the melody with chords or a bass line
questions.explain: The accompaniment supports the main melody, often with chords or a bass line.

options: Playing music you have not seen before, at first sight
questions.explain: Sight-reading is performing a piece of music you are seeing for the first time.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: What is the difference between a solo and an ensemble performance?
options: A solo is loud; an ensemble is quiet
A solo is one performer; an ensemble is a group
questions.explain: A solo is performed by one player, while an ensemble involves a group performing together.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: Using repetition when developing a musical idea helps to:
options: Make ideas memorable and give a sense of unity
questions.explain: Repetition makes musical ideas memorable and gives a piece unity and coherence.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.
